# 24. DevOps / CI-CD

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Make static-site release work repeatable, reviewable, and safe using free/open-source tooling and transparent automation.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A repository structure with source, public output, docs, tools, and generated reports clearly separated.
- [ ] A branch and release policy for production changes.
- [ ] A CI checklist using free-tier-friendly runners where available.
- [ ] Automated checks for links, HTML quality, accessibility basics, performance budgets, security patterns, and generated files where project complexity justifies it.
- [ ] A build command or no-build declaration.
- [ ] A deploy command or host integration record.
- [ ] A rollback procedure and release notes template.
- [ ] A secrets policy for CI tokens, deploy keys, analytics IDs, and form provider credentials.

## Must Be True
- [ ] CI must be reproducible from repository files and free/open-source tools.
- [ ] Generated files such as sitemap.xml must be updated by automation or clearly reviewed when changed manually.
- [ ] Failing checks must block launch-critical releases unless a documented exception exists.
- [ ] CI must not require paid private services for basic quality gates.
- [ ] Deploy previews must be protected from indexing.
- [ ] Secrets must be stored only in approved secret stores, never in static files.
- [ ] Automation must produce readable reports for non-developer stakeholders when needed.
- [ ] Manual deploy steps must be documented enough to repeat.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check CI from a clean clone, not only a local machine.
- [ ] Check that scripts work on common environments without hidden global dependencies.
- [ ] Check that build output does not include source-only files.
- [ ] Check that reports are retained or attached to releases where useful.
- [ ] Check that dependency installation uses lockfiles when dependencies exist.
- [ ] Check that deploy hooks cannot be triggered by untrusted changes without review.
- [ ] Check that production deploys use the intended branch and output directory.
- [ ] Check that local tooling versions are documented.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid CI that only runs formatting and misses functional launch risks.
- [ ] Avoid paid CI-only checks as mandatory gates for small static sites.
- [ ] Avoid storing provider tokens in repository files.
- [ ] Avoid deployments from unreviewed local folders.
- [ ] Avoid ignoring generated-file diffs.
- [ ] Avoid automation that is so opaque the client cannot maintain it.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] A release should be boring: checked, reviewed, deployed, smoke-tested, and reversible.
- [ ] CI/CD must improve confidence without creating vendor lock-in.
- [ ] The quality gate must reflect the site's risk profile.
- [ ] The repository must remain useful even if CI provider changes.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use the Python tool in CI for dependency-free baseline audits.
- [ ] Add optional free checks such as lychee, html-validate, pa11y-ci, Lighthouse CI, and Playwright as needed.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] DevOps strategy: clear workflow, source of truth, version control, repeatable deployment, safe updates, rollback, preview, tests, no one-machine dependency, and no paid deployment requirement.
- [ ] Repository workflow, source of truth, CI/CD pipeline, build-free checks, build-based static checks, environments, preview, production, rollback, automated QA, links/assets, accessibility gates, SEO gates, performance gates, security gates, forms, analytics, cookies/consent, multilingual, blog, portfolio, product/payment links, secrets, cache, DNS/domain, monitoring, release management, documentation, maintenance, red flags, and final approval are checked.
- [ ] Production deployment is controlled, preview is separate, failed checks block production where appropriate, logs do not expose secrets, and pipeline complexity matches project complexity.
- [ ] Release gates block exposed secrets, broken forms, broken HTTPS, mixed content, production robots blocking, localhost canonicals, missing critical metadata, and severe accessibility blockers.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
